title: Why Charging Slows Down After 80% 🔋 #shorts
desc: Your electric car and your phone charge fast to 80%, then crawl. Here's the simple reason, and a tip that saves time on every road trip.

scenes.text: Why does your car, and your phone, charge super fast to eighty percent, and then crawl?
Think of a battery as a giant parking lot. Charging means parking countless tiny lithium ions.
When the lot is almost empty, they rush in and park anywhere. That's the fast part.
But near eighty percent, free spots are hard to find. Push too hard, and the ions pile up outside.
That pile-up makes heat, and it can damage the battery forever.
So the charger slows down on purpose, to protect it.
Road trip tip: unplug at eighty and go. It's faster! Follow Bolt for a new 'why' every day!
